newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Jan-Feb trade gap falls 24 percent - official.
newsitem.headline: Peru Jan-Feb trade gap falls 24 percent - official.

text.p: Peru's trade deficit fell 24 percent in the first two months of the year to $210 million from $275 million in the same period last year, the government's official newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The daily El Peruano said exports were $1.035 billion in the first two months and imports were $1.243 billion in the same period. The report did not give comparative figures.
The official gazette said the information for the trade deficit figures came from "economic authorities", without eleborating.
Earlier this month the Customs Service announced the trade deficit for the first two months was down 24.9 percent to $213.5 million.

The Customs Service does not include all statistics used to calculate the country's official trade balance figures, which the Central Reserve Bank publishes. The bank was set to issue the January-February figures April 18.
Peru's trade deficit fell 9.0 percent in 1996 to $1.996 billion from $2.185 billion in 1995, according to the bank.
